messages.content: I have a mild fever and headache

Summary: Assessment of symptoms: 'I have a mild fever and headache' for age group: 18-64 years (Adult).

Home Care: • Drink plenty of fluids (water, warm broth, or herbal teas).
• Get adequate rest and monitor temperature.
• Avoid strenuous physical activities until feeling better.

Medical Attention: Consult a healthcare provider or seek urgent care if symptoms suddenly worsen, if fever persists above 102°F (39°C), or if you develop chest tightness or breathing trouble.

Possible Causes: Common viral illness, mild seasonal infection, or fatigue. A doctor's clinical evaluation is recommended for persistent symptoms.

I have a severe throbbing headache and light sensitivity

Summary: Reported head pain/headache in 18-64 years (Adult). Symptoms indicate cranial or myofascial discomfort, commonly presenting as tension-type pressure or unilateral pulsating migraine.

Home Care: • Rest in a quiet, darkened room free from screen glare and loud noises.
• Apply a cold damp washcloth to your forehead or temples, or a warm heating pad to tight neck muscles.
• Hydrate generously with 500-750 ml of water or electrolyte fluid.
• Practice gentle neck and shoulder rotations to relieve muscular tension.

Medical Attention: 🚨 Seek urgent medical evaluation if you experience:
• Sudden, explosive 'thunderclap' headache reaching maximum intensity in seconds.
• Headache accompanied by a stiff neck, high fever, or confusion.
• Any sudden focal numbness, weakness on one side of face/body, or speech difficulty.
• Headache following recent head trauma.

Possible Causes: Tension-type headache (stress, muscle contraction), migraine with or without aura, dehydration, prolonged eye strain, or sinus congestion.

I have an intense toothache and swollen gums

Summary: Reported dental or oral discomfort in 18-64 years (Adult). Indicates pulp irritation, gingival inflammation, or enamel compromise.

Home Care: • Rinse mouth thoroughly with warm salt water (1/2 tsp salt in 1 cup warm water) after eating.
• Apply a tiny drop of clove oil on a clean cotton swab directly onto the aching tooth area.
• Hold an ice pack wrapped in a cloth against the outside of your cheek for 10-15 minutes.
• Avoid very hot, icy, or sugary food items; sleep with head elevated on pillows.

Medical Attention: 🚨 Contact a dentist or urgent clinic urgently if you notice:
• Visible facial or jaw swelling extending toward the eye or neck.
• High fever accompanied by tooth pain or foul-tasting discharge (suspected abscess).
• Difficulty swallowing or opening the mouth wide.

Possible Causes: Dental caries (cavity), acute pulpitis, periodontal or periapical abscess, cracked tooth, or erupting wisdom tooth.
Severe stomach cramps with nausea and vomiting

Summary: Reported gastrointestinal disturbance (stomach pain/nausea/digestive upset) in 18-64 years (Adult). Suggests gastric mucosal irritation or intestinal inflammation.

Home Care: • Sip small volumes of Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) or electrolyte solutions frequently.
• Adopt the gentle BRAT diet: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, and plain Toast.
• Sip ginger tea or peppermint infusion to ease nausea and intestinal spasms.
• AVOID spicy, greasy, dairy-heavy foods and NSAID painkillers (like ibuprofen) which irritate stomach lining.

Medical Attention: 🚨 Seek urgent clinical attention if you develop:
• Sharp, severe localized pain in the lower right abdomen (suspected appendicitis).
• Vomiting blood or material resembling dark coffee grounds.
• Black, tarry stools or visible blood in bowel movements.
• Inability to keep fluids down for over 12 hours leading to dry mouth and no urination.

Possible Causes: Viral gastroenteritis ('stomach flu'), mild food poisoning, acute gastritis or acid reflux (GERD), dietary intolerance, or irritable bowel syndrome.
I have an itchy red skin rash and hives after eating nuts

Summary: Reported dermatological/skin symptoms (rash/itching/hives) in 18-64 years (Adult). Suggests epidermal inflammation, contact sensitivity, or allergic reaction.

Home Care: • Apply a clean, cool, damp compress to soothe itching and inflammation.
• Apply calamine lotion or pure fragrance-free moisturizer/aloe vera gel.
• Wear loose, smooth cotton clothing to minimize friction.
• Trim nails and avoid scratching to prevent secondary bacterial infection.

Medical Attention: 🚨 EMERGENCY (Anaphylaxis Risk): Seek immediate emergency care if skin rash is accompanied by swelling of lips, tongue, or throat, dizziness, or wheezing/difficulty breathing.
• Also seek prompt care for target-shaped 'bullseye' rash or rapidly spreading purple spots.

Possible Causes: Contact dermatitis (soap/plant/metal reaction), allergic urticaria (hives), atopic eczema, heat rash, or viral exanthem.

i have fever

Summary: Reported fever/temperature elevation in 13-17 years (Adolescent). Represents an active systemic immune defense to combat pathogens.

Home Care: • Maintain generous fluid intake with oral rehydration salts, broths, and water to prevent dehydration.
• Wear light, breathable cotton clothing and keep room temperature comfortably cool.
• Sponge face, neck, and arms with lukewarm water (never ice water or alcohol rubs).
• Ensure complete physical rest to conserve metabolic energy.

Medical Attention: 🚨 Consult a doctor promptly if:
• Temperature exceeds 103°F (39.4°C) or fails to respond after 48-72 hours.
• Fever is accompanied by a stiff neck, dark purple non-blanching rash, or confusion.
• Patient exhibits extreme lethargy, unresponsive behavior, or persistent vomiting.

Possible Causes: Acute viral infection (influenza, viral fever), bacterial infection, urinary tract infection, or post-vaccination immune response.

Summary: CLINICAL ASSESSMENT FOR 18-64 YEARS (ADULT) PATIENT:
Based on reported symptoms (Fever, Headache), the primary suspected condition is **COVID-19 (Coronavirus)** with a calculated **20.0% clinical match**.
Differential considerations include: Acute Bronchitis (17.9%), Typhoid Fever (14.3%).

Home Care: • Isolate in a well-ventilated room to prevent transmission.
• Monitor SpO2 with a pulse oximeter every 4-6 hours.
• Warm saline gargles and steam inhalation for throat relief.
• Generous hydration and balanced, protein-rich nutrition.

Medical Attention: ⚠️ URGENCY LEVEL: MILD
Watch for the following Warning Signs:
• Oxygen saturation (SpO2) < 94%
• Persistent chest pressure
• Confusion
• Bluish lips/face

Clinical Recommendation: Seek emergency care if SpO2 drops below 94% or severe breathing difficulty occurs.

Possible Causes: Primary Pathophysiology: A contagious respiratory infection caused by SARS-CoV-2, ranging from mild cold-like symptoms to viral pneumonia.

Recommended Tests / Confirmation: Consult a physician for formal clinical verification and diagnostic confirmation.
